name: delay-whatif
title: Delay what-if
description: What-if impact of delaying one activity of a P6 project, computed in memory: the activity today, what drives it, where its float comes from, then the project finish, milestones, critical counts and the activities that move (the database is never written). Use when the user asks what happens if an activity is late or delayed.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: task_code
args.description: Activity ID of the activity to delay

args.name: delay_days
args.description: Delay in days of the activity's calendar, added to its remaining duration

template:
Delay what-if on project {project}: activity {task_code} delayed by {delay_days} d (days of its calendar, added to its remaining duration). The activity today, what drives it, where its float comes from, then the effect on the project finish, the milestones, the critical activities and the activities that move. The what-if runs in memory: nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages. Pass delay_days as a number.
1. act = p6_get_activity(project="{project}", task_code="{task_code}"): the activity today.
2. drv = p6_driving_path(project="{project}", target="{task_code}", limit=15): what drives it.
3. fo = p6_float_origin(project="{project}", task_code="{task_code}", limit=10): where its total float comes from. If this call returns an error, keep its message as fo.error (its other fields are null).
4. wi = p6_schedule_whatif(project="{project}", edits=[{"op": "duration", "task_code": "{task_code}", "add_remaining_days": {delay_days}}], limit=15): the delay applied in memory.

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- The finish change is the delta field of the what-if: never work it out from two dates.

Nothing is changed in P6. To make the delay real, the user edits the activity in P6 (or with
p6_update_activity after their explicit yes) and reschedules (F9).

files.text:
# Delay what-if: {task_code} - {act_name} delayed by {delay_days} d

Project {project}. Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. The delay is added to the remaining duration and the schedule is computed again in memory by P6 MCP's CPM engine: nothing is written to the database. Before = the last F9 as stored.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. The stored dates and float are out of date, so the before values and the what-if are too, until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

[if not: engine_trusted]
Warning: the CPM engine does not reproduce the last F9 of this project ({engine_mismatched} open activities differ). The what-if figures are approximate: check them in P6 before relying on them.
[end if]

## The activity today

- {task_code} - {act_name}: status {act_status}, WBS {act_wbs}, calendar {act_calendar}.
- Actual start {act_actual_start}; early start {act_es}, early finish {act_ef}; late finish {act_lf}.
- Original duration {act_orig_d} d, remaining duration {act_rem_d} d, physical % complete {act_pct}.
- Total float {act_tf} d, free float {act_ff} d; on the longest path: {act_longest}.

## What drives it

Driving predecessors on the early dates of the last F9 (level 0 is the activity; completed activities are left out):

[table: drivers]

Each driving chain starts from:

[table: roots]

## Where its float comes from

[if: fo_error]
The float origin is not available: {fo_error}
[end if]

[if: origin_type]
Origin of the late dates: {origin_type}, at {origin_activity}, date {origin_date}.

{explanation}
[end if]

## Impact of the delay

- Edit applied: {edit_applied}.
- Project finish: before {finish_before}, after {finish_after}; change {finish_delta_cd} cd, {finish_delta_wd} wd (working days of the finish activity's calendar).
- Critical open activities ({fc_definition}): {critical_before} before, {critical_after} after; {became_critical} become critical, {no_longer_critical} are no longer critical.
- Open activities with negative float: {negative_before} before, {negative_after} after.
- Activities whose dates or float move: {changed_total}.

[if: finish_delta_cd]
Warning: this delay moves the project finish by {finish_delta_wd} wd.
[end if]

[if not: finish_delta_cd]
The project finish does not move: the delay is absorbed by float.
[end if]

### Finish activity and constrained activities

[table: milestones]

### Activities that become critical

[table: became]

### Activities that move, largest finish change first

[table: changed]

## Next step

Nothing was changed in P6: this what-if ran in memory. To make the delay real, change the activity in P6 (or ask for p6_update_activity, which is applied only after your explicit yes), then reschedule the project in P6 (F9).

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_get_activity says the activity is not found: "Activity <task_code> was not found in <project>: check the Activity ID (p6_query_activities)."
- act.status_code is TK_Complete: "<task_code> - <name> is completed: it has no remaining duration to delay." Do not run the what-if.
- p6_schedule_whatif returns an error: repeat its message and stop.

## Warnings (fixed sentences of report.md)

- schedule_state.stale is true: keep the warning that the project changed after its last F9.
- wi.engine.trusted is false: keep the warning that the engine does not reproduce the last F9.
- fo returned an error (fo.error not null): keep its sentence instead of the float origin.
- wi.project_finish.delta_cd is not 0: keep the warning that the delay moves the project finish.

## Cross-checks (each pair must be equal)

1. act.schedule_state.data_date = drv.data_date = wi.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. act.schedule_state.data_date = fo.schedule_state.data_date (skip when fo returned an error).
3. act.total_float_d = drv.target.total_float_d.
4. act.total_float_d = fo.activity.total_float_d (skip when fo returned an error).
5. act.early_end_date = drv.target.early_finish.
6. fo.project_finish = wi.project_finish.before (skip when fo returned an error).

If a pair differs, the database changed between the calls: run the four calls again once. If it still
differs, say which pair differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The finish change comes from wi.project_finish.delta_cd and delta_wd, never from two dates.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (drivers 15, chain starts 10,
  milestones 10, become critical 15, activities that move 15). A table whose call has more pages
  (next_offset not null) ends with its line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> ...", both numbers
  copied from that call.
- Every activity is written "Activity ID - name".
- The report says that nothing was written: the what-if runs in memory. Any real change needs the
  user's explicit yes, then F9 in P6.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Delay what-if

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. act = p6_get_activity(project="{project}", task_code="{task_code}"): the activity today.
2. drv = p6_driving_path(project="{project}", target="{task_code}", limit=15): what drives it.
3. fo = p6_float_origin(project="{project}", task_code="{task_code}", limit=10): where its total float comes from. If this call returns an error, keep its message as fo.error (its other fields are null).
4. wi = p6_schedule_whatif(project="{project}", edits=[{"op": "duration", "task_code": "{task_code}", "add_remaining_days": {delay_days}}], limit=15): the delay applied in memory.

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {task_code}: Activity ID of the activity to delay, as given
- {delay_days}: Delay in days of the activity's calendar, added to its remaining duration, as given

## Units

- wd: working days of each activity's calendar
- cd: calendar days
- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- %: percent

## Table drivers

Level 0 = the activity, then its open driving predecessors.

Rows: drv.rows, in the order returned, at most 15.
